Done. All work is complete and every verification command exits 0.

## Changes

**`app.tsx`** — ThreadRow: `useIsCompactViewport()` gates three behaviours — the Inactive pill is gone at every width (pill renders only `!compact && status !== "inactive"`; on compact a non-inactive thread instead gets a `.pf-thread-state-dot` inside `.pf-provider`, `role="img"` with the translated `aria-label`); the ⋯ trigger renders only on the active row on compact; a 450 ms long-press inside the row link opens the same dropdown and swallows the following click/contextmenu (flag clears on next touchstart, 700 ms after firing, re-armed to 400 ms on touchend; cancels on move >10px, early end/cancel, second touch, rename, compact→desktop, unmount). Tree: compact `childrenStyle` fixes the six logical properties (level step = 7px + 1px guide), `.pf-chats` margin 0, `--pf-indent` not assigned on compact, and «Новый проект» is an icon-only ghost button (aria-label only — see note) that stays the first child button.

**`style.css`** — `.pf-thread-state-dot` (8px circle, `border-width: 0`, `background: currentColor`, surface ring, `inset-inline-end` so RTL mirrors), `.pf-provider` gets `position: relative`, and the phone media query gives `.pf-tree .pf-thread a` / `.pf-tree .pf-heading .pf-label` `align-self: stretch; min-height: inherit` after the `.pf-compact` rules (row heights unchanged).

**`i18n.tsx`** — language precedence: saved choice > `html lang` ru > `navigator.language` primary subtag (if supported) > en; storage failure = no saved choice; absent navigator guarded.

**Tests** — new `mobile-compact.test.tsx` (13 tests covering all acceptance points with fake timers) and `i18n.test.ts` extended to a jsdom test of the precedence chain including the storage-failure path. `thread-row/chat-actions/panel` tests needed no changes — none asserted the Inactive pill.

**One plan deviation**: plan point 5 wants the compact button to carry `title` as well as `aria-label`, but the project's `Button` deliberately omits `title` from its props (`Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes, "title">` in components/ui/button.tsx), so only `aria-label` is set — which is what acceptance item 8 checks.

**NOT RUN**: none — all three contract commands ran green here: `npx vitest run mobile-compact.test.tsx` (13 passed), `npx vitest run thread-row.test.tsx chat-actions.test.tsx panel.test.tsx i18n.test.ts tree-layout.test.ts thread-status.test.ts` (56 passed), `npx tsc --noEmit` (exit 0). Also ran the full suite (42 files / 358 tests) — no sibling breakage.

Changed paths: `app.tsx`, `style.css`, `i18n.tsx`, `i18n.test.ts`, `mobile-compact.test.tsx` (new)

APPROACH: implemented compact gating entirely through `useIsCompactViewport()` per the locked decisions, kept desktop code paths byte-identical except the Inactive-pill removal, proved each acceptance point in `mobile-compact.test.tsx` with the shared `installTestMatchMedia` mock and vitest fake timers, and debugged the one flaky-feeling failure (leftover swallow timer) by instrumenting schedule/clear sites until the root cause surfaced: alternating `vi.useRealTimers()`/`vi.useFakeTimers()` in one test leaves a stale clock whose ids the fresh clock cannot clear — restructured the unmount test onto a single clock.

LESSON: when a timer-count assertion crosses a vitest clock reinstall, the second `useFakeTimers` install reuses a global id counter but not the old clock's timer map — keep one fake-clock lifecycle per test and flush async data loads with `await act(async () => {})` instead of `findBy*` once fake timers are active.

APPROACH: mobile-only behaviour concentrated behind `useIsCompactViewport()` in ThreadRow/Tree, dot reuses the existing `.pf-state-*` colour classes, geometry set inline per the reviewed contract, language precedence rewritten in `preference()`, and every acceptance item asserted in `mobile-compact.test.tsx` with fake timers; desktop output stays as before except the removed Inactive pill.

LESSON: alternating `vi.useRealTimers()`/`vi.useFakeTimers()` inside one test leaves timers stranded on the uninstalled clock (ids continue globally but the map does not) — drive all fake-timer scenarios through a single clock install and swap real timers only between tests.
